chapters.title: Small Enough to Say Yes To
chapters.tease: A small engagement asks a stranger to risk a little on a specific result by a date. A yes they can give.

chapters.title: Sell Outcomes, Not Hours
chapters.tease: Day rates punish you for getting faster with Claude. Price the outcome and the speed becomes yours to keep.

chapters.title: The Diagnostic Call
chapters.tease: The first call is a diagnosis, not a pitch. The expensive problem arrives around question twelve.

chapters.title: The Paid Audit
chapters.tease: A fixed-scope paid audit is the best front door: it ends with a roadmap only you are placed to deliver.

chapters.title: The Two-Week Sprint
chapters.tease: Two weeks, one problem, one working result: long enough to ship, short enough that momentum survives.

chapters.title: Name the Thing
chapters.tease: An unnamed service is a favour. A named one is a product with a price, and a shape that resists sprawl.

chapters.title: One Vertical, Deep
chapters.tease: Generalists compete with everyone. A specialist arrives with scoping half done and becomes the obvious call.

chapters.title: Productise the Repeatable
chapters.tease: The third time you build the same thing, it is a product. Write the playbook and the effort curve bends.

chapters.title: Pilot to Retainer
chapters.tease: Useful AI systems need looking after. Design what happens after the pilot succeeds before the pilot starts.

chapters.title: The Offer Ladder
chapters.tease: Teardown, audit, sprint, retainer: a ladder where each rung makes the next feel inevitable.

chapters.title: Brief Like a Client
chapters.tease: Brief Claude the way you wish clients briefed you: context, task, format and the check most people skip.

chapters.title: Role, Task, Format
chapters.tease: Who is answering, what they must do and what shape it takes: three lines that fix most bad prompts.

chapters.title: Show Three Examples
chapters.tease: Style is faster to show than to describe. Three varied examples beat a paragraph of adjectives.

chapters.title: Negative Examples
chapters.tease: Show the output you do not want beside the one you do. The contrast teaches the boundary in one pass.

chapters.title: Constrain the Output
chapters.tease: An unconstrained model writes an essay. A constrained one writes data the next step can actually use.

chapters.title: Make It Think First
chapters.tease: On hard problems, quality comes from the loop: reason, draft, critique, revise. Not the first answer.

chapters.title: Ask for the Rubric
chapters.tease: Ask the model to write the marking scheme first, then answer, grade itself and revise to full marks.

chapters.title: Prefill the Answer
chapters.tease: Start the reply yourself, with a bracket, heading or label, and the model continues in that shape.

chapters.title: Prompts Are Assets
chapters.tease: A prompt you use twenty times is infrastructure: it needs a name, a version, a home and tests.

chapters.title: Sell the Prompt Kit
chapters.tease: A prompt kit is the smallest thing you can sell that a team will use every single day.

chapters.title: Context Is the Product
chapters.tease: Model quality is roughly fixed. What you feed it is not, and choosing context is the expertise clients buy.

chapters.title: Paste the Real Thing
chapters.tease: Summaries lose exactly the detail that mattered. Paste the real thing, cleared and specific.

chapters.title: Order Matters
chapters.tease: Long documents first, your question last, so the instruction is fresh when the model starts to answer.

chapters.title: The Context Budget
chapters.tease: Context is a budget, not a container. Three right files beat thirty, and answers sharpen as the pile shrinks.

chapters.title: Long-Chat Rot
chapters.tease: Long conversations carry dead assumptions. Ask for a handover summary, correct it, and start again with it.

chapters.title: Project Knowledge
chapters.tease: Pin durable knowledge once, in a project per client, and every conversation starts from the right foundation.

chapters.title: Restate the Goal
chapters.tease: Long tasks drift one sensible step at a time. A twenty-word restatement of the goal pulls them back.

chapters.title: Kill Stale Context
chapters.tease: Stale context is not merely out of date. The model blends it into plausible hybrids that look right.

chapters.title: Structured Input
chapters.tease: Wrap each kind of material in a named tag, refer to the tags in your task, and keep untrusted text as data.

chapters.title: The Documentation Sprint
chapters.tease: A documentation sprint turns knowledge in people’s heads into guides a new hire and a model can both use.

chapters.title: Read the Repo First
chapters.tease: Before the first edit in a client’s repository, ask Claude Code for the map. Ten minutes buys hours.

chapters.title: CLAUDE.md First
chapters.tease: Your first commit in a client repo should be CLAUDE.md: the page the agent reads before anything else.

chapters.title: Plan Before the Edit
chapters.tease: Have the agent write the plan before touching a file. A wrong plan costs seconds; a bad refactor, hours.

chapters.title: Small Diffs, Fast Loops
chapters.tease: One concern per turn, verified before the next. Small diffs fail in ways you can simply undo.

chapters.title: Let It Run the Tests
chapters.tease: Give Claude Code the test command and it stops guessing: it runs, reads failures, adjusts and proves it.

chapters.title: Git Is the Undo Button
chapters.tease: Commit before you let an agent loose. A clean tree turns every bad session into a two-second reset.

chapters.title: Custom Slash Commands
chapters.tease: Any workflow you run twice in Claude Code should become a named, shared slash command.

chapters.title: Connectors as Hands
chapters.tease: Connectors give Claude hands in real systems. Scope every one by least privilege, and write it down.

chapters.title: Headless in CI
chapters.tease: Run Claude Code headless in CI and every pull request gets a review before a human spends judgement on it.

chapters.title: The Workflow Fix
chapters.tease: One painful, recurring workflow, diagnosed, fixed with Claude Code, verified, handed over and measured.

chapters.title: Skills Beat Prompts
chapters.tease: A prompt has to be found and pasted. A skill loads itself when the task calls for it.

chapters.title: The Trigger Description
chapters.tease: A skill that never fires is worthless. Its description is the trigger: write it in the language of requests.

chapters.title: Progressive Disclosure
chapters.tease: Keep a short core that every use needs, and put the detail in references read only when needed.

chapters.title: Bundle the Scripts
chapters.tease: Deterministic work belongs in code, not tokens. The model brings judgement; a bundled script, precision.

chapters.title: Subagent Fan-Out
chapters.tease: Split independent work across subagents with clean contexts, then synthesise one consistent shape.

chapters.title: The Verifier Subagent
chapters.tease: One agent builds; a second checks with fresh eyes, seeing only the work and the criteria.

chapters.title: One Skill, Many Harnesses
chapters.tease: A skill that runs in the app, Claude Code, a scheduled job and the platform is an asset that compounds.

chapters.title: Version Your Canon
chapters.tease: Skills drift into rival copies. Keep one versioned canon in git and let changes flow outwards from it.

chapters.title: Skills as Deliverable
chapters.tease: Clients pay for outcomes but keep assets. A skill library does the work itself, every day, to their standard.

chapters.title: The Agent Pilot
chapters.tease: An agent pilot is an experiment on last month’s real work, with a threshold set first and an honest result.

chapters.title: The Demo Is the Deck
chapters.tease: A working prototype closes deals that slides can only describe. Showing is now cheaper than explaining.

chapters.title: Single-File Prototypes
chapters.tease: One file, no build step, runs anywhere. That constraint is the secret to fast prototypes.

chapters.title: Fake Data, Real Feel
chapters.tease: Realistic sample data makes a prototype persuasive. Placeholder text makes it a wireframe.

chapters.title: Screenshot to Spec
chapters.tease: Clients cannot always say what they want, but they can point at it. Make the screenshot the brief.

chapters.title: The Clickable Prototype
chapters.tease: Half-real beats fully imagined. Three working flows and honest stubs answer more than any specification.

chapters.title: One Artifact per Question
chapters.tease: Resist the mega-app. One artifact that answers one business question gets used every week, for years.

chapters.title: A Link Beats an Attachment
chapters.tease: Send a link, not a file. A link travels through an organisation; an attachment waits in an inbox.

chapters.title: The Leave-Behind
chapters.tease: One artifact, two outputs: interactive on screen, and a tidy document on paper through print styles.

chapters.title: Verify Before You Claim
chapters.tease: Never say it works until you have run it. Evidence before assertion is what keeps you trusted.

chapters.title: Ship in the Meeting
chapters.tease: Build the change live while the buyer watches. It converts scepticism faster than any deck.

chapters.title: Week One Is Access
chapters.tease: Nothing ships until you have logins, data access and a named decision-maker. Chase all three on day one.

chapters.title: Guardrails over Guesswork
chapters.tease: Decide up front what the agent may never do, then enforce it in the system, not in a hopeful prompt.

chapters.title: Human in the Loop
chapters.tease: Design the human checkpoint deliberately. Autonomy is earned per action type, on evidence.

chapters.title: Evals as Acceptance
chapters.tease: Replace vague sign-off with a scored test set. Acceptance by score invites a fix, not an argument.

chapters.title: Demo Every Friday
chapters.tease: A weekly demo is the cheapest insurance against building the wrong thing.

chapters.title: The Scope Creep Protocol
chapters.tease: Say yes to the idea and no to the timeline. Every new request gets a same-day change note.

chapters.title: Write the Runbook
chapters.tease: The system you leave must be operable by someone who has never met you. The runbook is how.

chapters.title: Train the Champion
chapters.tease: Every account needs one insider who can demonstrate the system without you, or adoption quietly dies.

chapters.title: Hand Over the Prompts
chapters.tease: Hand over everything built from the client's context. Your method stays yours; their work is theirs.

chapters.title: Close the Loop Loudly
chapters.tease: Quantify what changed and tell the buyer in their language. Unmeasured wins do not get renewed.

chapters.title: Price the Value Gap
chapters.tease: Anchor the price on what the problem costs the client, not on what the work costs you.

chapters.title: Never Quote First
chapters.tease: Ask what the client has allocated before you name a number. Then shape the scope to fit.

chapters.title: Three Options Always
chapters.tease: One price invites a yes or a no. Three options move the question from whether to which.

chapters.title: Charge for Discovery
chapters.tease: Free scoping trains buyers to treat your thinking as a sample. Charge for the investigation.

chapters.title: Deposit Before Access
chapters.tease: Work begins when money moves. A deposit and complete access are both preconditions for the start.

chapters.title: Setup Plus Monthly
chapters.tease: Charge properly for the build, then charge again to keep it alive. Recurring care makes a business.

chapters.title: Know Your Token Cost
chapters.tease: Agentic delivery has a real marginal cost. Track it per client before a fixed price becomes a loss.

chapters.title: Raise on Renewal
chapters.tease: Every renewal is a repricing decision. Open with documented value, then decide on purpose.

chapters.title: Cash Beats Equity
chapters.tease: When a start-up offers shares instead of a fee, take the money. Cash runs the practice.

chapters.title: Fire the Bad Accounts
chapters.tease: The client who pays least and asks most is blocking the one who would pay most.

chapters.title: Case Study per Job
chapters.tease: Write the case study while the numbers are warm and the client delighted. Twenty minutes, two years of proof.

chapters.title: Referral by Design
chapters.tease: Ask for referrals at the moment of maximum delight, and ask for one specific introduction.

chapters.title: The Teardown Email
chapters.tease: Do the work before the meeting. A teardown email shows a prospect a real opening and a concrete fix.

chapters.title: Ship a Free Tool
chapters.tease: A small, useful tool in your niche is the best business card ever invented. It works while you sleep.

chapters.title: Build in Public
chapters.tease: Ship something visible every week. Buyers hire the person whose work they have watched for three months.

chapters.title: Talk at the Meetup
chapters.tease: Twenty engaged people in a room beat two thousand impressions online. Give a practical talk.

chapters.title: Own Your Niche Search
chapters.tease: Be listed everywhere your specific buyer looks. Boring distribution beats brilliant content nobody finds.

chapters.title: Publish the Waitlist
chapters.tease: When you are genuinely fully booked, publish the next start date. Buyers move from whether to when.

chapters.title: Warm Beats Cold
chapters.tease: Your last five clients know everyone you want to meet. Systematic, useful follow-up beats any cold channel.

chapters.title: Write the Playbook
chapters.tease: Publishing your method costs almost nothing and makes you the obvious person to hire.

chapters.title: Sell Systems, Not Sessions
chapters.tease: A session ends when you log off. A system keeps producing at three in the morning. Sell systems.

chapters.title: Agents That Report Their Value
chapters.tease: The next tier is a system that runs the workflow and reports its own value, every month, unasked.

chapters.title: Own the Eval Layer
chapters.tease: As models get cheaper and better, the scarce skill is knowing whether their output is good.

chapters.title: Upgrades Are Free R&D
chapters.tease: Every model release can improve what you already shipped, if you have built for it and kept evals ready.

chapters.title: Compounding Side Builds
chapters.tease: Every build should reuse the last one's parts. Two years of that is a library nobody catches in a quarter.

chapters.title: The Skill Library Moat
chapters.tease: Anyone can buy the model. Nobody else has your encoded workflows, tuned on real client work.

chapters.title: Fleet over Flagship
chapters.tease: Ten small engagements earning steadily beat one heroic bet on a flagship client.

chapters.title: The Two-Person Practice
chapters.tease: Agentic delivery means headcount stops tracking capacity. Two people can now have remarkable reach.

chapters.title: Teach It to Replace You
chapters.tease: Encode every repeatable judgement into a skill. The goal is capacity you can sell twice.

chapters.title: Judgement Is the Last Job
chapters.tease: Sell small, deliver fast, prove it, earn the next yes, and keep the judgement for yourself.
